This is the completed round trip that killed SAIC and NTNX, arriving on day 2.
entryWatch.why: THIS IS WHAT A PRE-REGISTERED TEST IS FOR. The 9/2 file wrote that OLLI was worth the 9/3 and 9/4 opens' attention IF IT BUILT A SHELF, on the same terms SAIC was given and failed and MDT was given and passed. The test was written yesterday with nothing at stake, applied this morning, and it DISQUALIFIED THE NAME THIS BOARD EXPECTED TO BUY. A 22.4% beat - 1.42 against 1.16 - is not the question; the question was whether the gap held its pre-print close, and it did not. Recorded prominently because the alternative reading, that the board went looking for a reason to prefer the name it already owned an opinion on, is the failure this row exists to rule out.

MDT's 11/17 print clears a 3-6 week expiry outright, so for once the no-earnings-hold rule did not settle the question first and the spread had to answer it. THE LIQUID 10/16 MONTHLY WAS THEN TESTED RATHER THAN SKIPPED: 92.5c 2.51/3.55, mark 3.03, 34.3% of mark, OI 843, delta 0.514; 90c 3.85/5.40, mark 4.625, 33.5%, OI 1550, delta 0.635. All quoted live at 13:46Z.
entryWatch.why: THIS IS A STRONGER STATEMENT OF THE FINDING THAN THE SMALL-CAP VERSIONS IT HAS RESTED ON. Affordability PASSES - 303 and 463 against 1011.15 deployable. Delta PASSES - 0.514 and 0.635 against a 0.40 floor. Expiry PASSES. Earnings-clearance PASSES. Open interest PASSES at 843 and 1550. ONLY SPREAD FAILS, and it fails by more than three times the ceiling on a mega-cap's most liquid monthly. The 2026-08-10 rule change said the deposit answered the affordability half of the option finding and none of the spread half, and that options become available when a chain quotes inside 10% rather than when the account grows. This is that claim tested properly rather than assumed: no balance narrows a 34% spread, and equity on the identical name quotes 0.141%. Refusing options without checking the expiry that actually carries the open interest would have been a weak test, so the monthly was pulled.

entryWatch.trigger: STILL REFUSED, BUT THE REFUSAL NOW COSTS SOMETHING. SAIC is 125.88 bid / 127.44 ask at 2026-09-03T13:42:46.012185728Z, last 126.83, -0.28% against a 127.18 settled close. It closed 9/2 at 127.18 - which is ABOVE its 125.96 pre-print close - having been 123.50 and breaking down when this board quoted it yesterday. So the name the board used for five sessions as its worked example of a failed beat has turned and reclaimed the exact line the example was built on. Refused today on a 1.23% spread, nine times MDT's, and because three lower sessions followed by one bounce is not a base.
entryWatch.why: MOVED FROM DEAD TO WATCH AND SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. SAIC was this board's control case: a 30.9% beat that round-tripped its pre-print close on day 2 and kept going, cited repeatedly as the reason MDT was bought instead. That comparison is now weaker than it was, because SAIC recovered. It does NOT invalidate the test - the test is about what the tape does with the gap, and SAIC did lose the line for three sessions before reclaiming it, which is a different and worse path than never losing it. But a board that cites a control case while it flatters the argument and stops updating it when it turns is running an advertisement. So it is updated on the hour it looks wrong.
